interest: Shows Japanese banks relying on American caretakers during the 1937 Tsingtao evacuation, and Yokohama Specie Bank's 1939 Tientsin expansion.
overview: In August 1937, the Yokohama Specie Bank and Bank of Chosen entrusted their Tsingtao property to an American businessman during the Japanese evacuation; in January 1939, Tientsin's Consul General reported the bank opened a branch in the Japanese concession while keeping its main office in the British concession.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a telegram from Tsingtao regarding the safeguarding of Japanese bank properties by an American businessman during the evacuation.
subfiles.summary: Indexes an August 1937 telegram: during Japan's Tsingtao evacuation, two Japanese banks asked an American to safeguard their property.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Telegram from Tsingtao on Japanese Bank Property

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet citing a Navy Department communication concerning Japanese bank properties in Tsingtao.
subfiles.summary: Indexes an August 1937 Navy report confirming that two Japanese banks asked an American to safeguard their Tsingtao property.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Navy Department Report on Japanese Banks in Tsingtao

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting that the Yokohama Specie Bank opened a branch in the Japanese concession in Tientsin while keeping its main office in the British concession.
subfiles.summary: Caldwell reports Tientsin press news that the Yokohama Specie Bank opened a branch in the Japanese concession on January 5, 1939, while keeping its main office in the British concession for now.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Caldwell (Tientsin) on Yokohama Specie Bank Branch Opening
